text: The orca is the ocean's top predator. So it wins, right?
Antarctica, 2009. Orcas knocked a seal off an ice floe.
Then a humpback swam in, and the seal ended up resting on the humpback's chest.
Scientist Robert Pitman started collecting cases.
He found one hundred fifteen encounters between humpbacks and hunting orcas, from 1951 to 2012.
In only about one in ten, the humpbacks were protecting their own calves.
The rest? Seals. Sea lions. Gray whales. Even a sunfish.
They trumpet, slap their giant flippers, and charge in, sometimes from far away.
Humpbacks are the only whales known to drive orcas off.
Why do they do it? Maybe they just hear orcas hunting, and come to break it up.
Would you call that a hero?
